title: Conformal anomaly in a vector field model with auxiliary scalar field
summary: The conformal anomaly has well-known ambiguities related to the possible schemes of regularization and renormalization. In case of dimensional regularization, one of the options is to formulate the theory as conformal in the dimension $D \neq 4$. For a gauge vector field this can be done in several ways and one of the options is to introduce an auxiliary scalar playing the role of a compensator. The advantage of this approach is that it preserves gauge symmetry and avoids problems with possible violation of unitarity. We explore the consequences of introducing such an auxiliary field for the anomaly and anomaly-induced action. It is shown that the new scalar degree of freedom gains an independent dynamics after taking the $4D$ limit. The remnant scalar, also, demonstrates some interesting properties.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the introduction of an auxiliary scalar compensator field in dimensional regularization to preserve conformal symmetry and gauge invariance for vector fields in D≠4, finding that this scalar gains independent dynamics in the 4D limit and exhibits interesting properties related to the conformal anomaly.
AI.motivation: The conformal anomaly has well-known ambiguities depending on regularization/renormalization schemes. The authors aim to explore a method that preserves gauge symmetry and avoids unitarity violation when formulating a conformal gauge vector theory in D≠4 using dimensional regularization.
AI.method: The approach introduces an auxiliary scalar field acting as a compensator to maintain conformal symmetry for a gauge vector field in D≠4 dimensions within dimensional regularization, then takes the 4D limit to examine the consequences.
AI.result: The new scalar degree of freedom acquires independent dynamics after taking the 4D limit. The remnant scalar demonstrates interesting properties in the context of the conformal anomaly and anomaly-induced action.
AI.conclusion: Introducing a compensator scalar to preserve conformal symmetry and gauge invariance in D≠4 leads to a dynamically independent scalar in 4D with notable features related to the conformal anomaly, offering a viable approach that avoids gauge symmetry issues and unitarity violation.

title: Fusion of Integrable Defects and the Defect $g$-Function
summary: We study exact defect $g$-functions for integrable line defects in two-dimensional integrable quantum field theory and use them to probe defect fusion. We consider three settings: fusion of purely transmitting topological defects, fusion of non-topological defects with reflection and transmission, and fusion of a defect with an integrable boundary. For topological defects, the separated logarithmic $g$-function is additive, and the fusion limit is controlled by the multiplicative composition of transmission factors. For non-topological defects, separation-dependent phases in the Bethe-Yang equations produce oscillatory finite-size effects, while the fused defect is described by effective reflection and transmission amplitudes. In the Ising examples studied here, fusion involving non-topological defects lowers the finite localized contribution to the entropy, whereas topological defect-boundary fusion leaves it unchanged.

AI.tldr: This paper studies exact defect g-functions for integrable line defects in 2D quantum field theory, examining defect fusion in three settings: topological defects, non-topological defects with reflection/transmission, and defect-boundary fusion, with Ising model examples showing entropy effects.
AI.motivation: To understand defect fusion in integrable quantum field theories through the lens of exact defect g-functions, probing how defects combine and how their finite-size contributions to entropy behave.
AI.method: Analytical study of defect g-functions in three settings: topological defect fusion (transmission factors), non-topological defects (Bethe-Yang equations with separation-dependent phases), and defect-boundary fusion, with Ising model as a testbed.
AI.result: For topological defects, the separated logarithmic g-function is additive and fusion is controlled by multiplicative transmission factors. For non-topological defects, oscillatory finite-size effects arise from separation-dependent phases, and fusion is described by effective reflection/transmission amplitudes. In the Ising model, non-topological defect fusion lowers finite localized entropy, while topological defect-boundary fusion leaves it unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The behavior of defect g-functions under fusion depends strongly on defect type: topological defects exhibit additive g-functions and unchanged entropy under boundary fusion, while non-topological defects reduce entropy upon fusion.

title: Comprehensive study of hidden charm pentaquarks with an improved unitarization method
summary: This work investigates dynamically generated hidden-charm baryon resonances arising from meson-baryon interactions. Using the local hidden gauge formalism, we model the interaction via t-channel vector meson exchange and unitarize the amplitude using the Bethe-Salpeter equation. To address regularization issues, we propose a novel ``hybrid loop function'' scheme that eliminates the unphysical poles -- common artifacts in cutoff or dimensional regularization -- while keeping the predictions of physical states. Consequently, the model successfully reproduces six experimentally known hidden-charm pentaquarks as well as earlier theoretical results, and predicts new states in the S=-1, I=1 sector.

AI.tldr: The paper studies hidden-charm baryon resonances from meson-baryon interactions. Using the local hidden gauge formalism and Bethe-Salpeter equation, they introduce a "hybrid loop function" scheme to remove unphysical poles from regularization. The model reproduces six known hidden-charm pentaquarks and predicts new states in the S=-1, I=1 sector.
AI.motivation: To investigate dynamically generated hidden-charm baryon resonances and address regularization issues (unphysical poles) in cutoff or dimensional regularization methods used in meson-baryon interaction models.
AI.method: Local hidden gauge formalism for t-channel vector meson exchange interactions; Bethe-Salpeter equation for amplitude unitarization; a novel "hybrid loop function" scheme to eliminate unphysical poles.
AI.result: Successfully reproduces six experimentally known hidden-charm pentaquarks and matches earlier theoretical predictions; predicts new states in the S=-1, I=1 sector.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid loop function scheme effectively removes regularization artifacts while preserving physical predictions, validating the model and extending the spectrum of hidden-charm baryon resonances.

title: Integrable sigma models with Haantjes structure on ${H_{4}}$ Lie group
summary: By solving algebraic relations for the conditions of Haantjes structure on a Lie algebra ${\G}$ and by using the corresponding automorphism group we proceed to classify all inequivalent algebraic Haantjes structures on ${\G}$. In this manner, we obtain 34 inequivalent algebraic Haantjes structures on the ${h_{4}}$ Lie algebra. We deform the chiral sigma model on a Lie group by using Haantjes structure on it. Then we try to obtain conditions on this structure such that the deformed sigma model remains to be integrable. Finally, using the ${h_{4}}$ Haantjes structures and solving this conditions three new integrable sigma models on the ${H_{4}}$ Lie group are obtained.

AI.tldr: The paper classifies 34 inequivalent algebraic Haantjes structures on the h₄ Lie algebra, then uses them to deform chiral sigma models on the H₄ Lie group, finding conditions for integrability and producing three new integrable sigma models.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify algebraic Haantjes structures on Lie algebras and leverage them to construct new integrable deformations of sigma models.
AI.method: Solving algebraic relations for Haantjes structure conditions on a Lie algebra, using the automorphism group for classification, and imposing integrability conditions on deformed sigma models.
AI.result: 34 inequivalent algebraic Haantjes structures on h₄ were found; three new integrable sigma models on the H₄ Lie group were obtained.
AI.conclusion: Haantjes structures provide a systematic algebraic framework for constructing integrable deformations of sigma models, demonstrated explicitly on h₄/H₄.

title: $D^0$--$D_s^+$ elliptic-flow splitting from sequential hadronization in O--O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
summary: We investigate the elliptic-flow splitting between prompt $D^0$ and $D_s^+$ mesons in O--O and Pb--Pb collisions within a heavy-quark transport framework with sequential hadronization, in which $D_s^+$ forms at $1.2\,T_c$ and $D^0$ at $T_c$. We present predictions for the $p_T$-differential $v_2$ and $D_s^+/D^0$ yield ratio in O--O $0$--$20\%$ collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.36$~TeV. The sequential scenario reproduces the $v_2(D^0) > v_2(D_s^+)$ ordering observed in preliminary ALICE data and predicts an enhanced $D_s^+/D^0$ ratio at low $p_T$, whereas a simultaneous baseline yields the opposite $v_2$ ordering. The splitting in O--O is substantially smaller than in Pb--Pb $30$--$50\%$, which we trace to the competition between the initial geometric eccentricity and the duration of the $1.2\,T_c \to T_c$ evolution window. A systematic scan across nine collision configurations reveals a universal linear scaling between the hadronic splitting and the partonic flow increment accumulated during this window, establishing the $D^0$--$D_s^+$ flow splitting as a hadronization chronometer of the quark-gluon plasma.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts that sequential hadronization (D_s⁺ forms at 1.2 T_c, D⁰ at T_c) explains the v₂(D⁰) > v₂(D_s⁺) ordering seen in preliminary ALICE data and enhances the D_s⁺/D⁰ ratio at low p_T. The flow splitting is smaller in O–O than Pb–Pb collisions, scaling linearly with the partonic flow increment during the 1.2 T_c → T_c window, establishing it as a hadronization chronometer of the QGP.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanism behind the observed elliptic-flow splitting between prompt D⁰ and D_s⁺ mesons and to test whether sequential hadronization can explain the ordering v₂(D⁰) > v₂(D_s⁺) seen in preliminary ALICE data, thereby probing the hadronization temperature hierarchy of different charm hadrons.
AI.method: Heavy-quark transport framework with sequential hadronization (D_s⁺ forms at 1.2 T_c, D⁰ at T_c). The model is applied to O–O (0–20%, √s_NN = 5.36 TeV) and Pb–Pb (30–50%) collisions. A systematic scan across nine collision configurations is performed to extract scaling relations.
AI.result: Sequential hadronization reproduces the v₂(D⁰) > v₂(D_s⁺) ordering, while a simultaneous baseline yields the opposite. The D_s⁺/D⁰ ratio is enhanced at low p_T. Flow splitting in O–O is smaller than in Pb–Pb 30–50%. A universal linear scaling exists between the hadronic splitting and the partonic flow increment during the 1.2 T_c → T_c window.
AI.conclusion: The D⁰–D_s⁺ flow splitting can serve as a hadronization chronometer of the quark-gluon plasma, with the magnitude of the splitting controlled by the competition between initial geometric eccentricity and the duration of the sequential hadronization window.

title: Chaos-Integrability Transition in the BPS Subspace of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ SYK Model
summary: We study chaos-integrability transition purely within a BPS subspace of a specific supersymmetric model that interpolates between the chaotic $\mathcal{N}=2$ SYK model and an integrable $\mathcal{N}=2$ "commuting" SYK model. Using the framework of BPS chaos, we analyze the spectrum of an operator projected onto the BPS subspace. We numerically find that its spectral statistics exhibit random-matrix behavior near the SYK limit and smoothly transitions to Poisson statistics near the integrable limit. Our results provide a direct example of a chaos-integrability crossover diagnosed solely from BPS states.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the transition from chaos to integrability within a BPS subspace of a supersymmetric model that interpolates between chaotic and integrable SYK-like models, using BPS chaos and spectral statistics of projected operators to demonstrate the crossover.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether chaos-integrability transitions can be detected purely within BPS subspaces, without relying on the full Hilbert space dynamics.
AI.method: The authors consider a supersymmetric model interpolating between the chaotic N=2 SYK model and an integrable "commuting" SYK model. They project an operator onto the BPS subspace, analyze its spectral statistics using random matrix theory, and numerically track the transition from random-matrix (chaotic) to Poisson (integrable) behavior.
AI.result: The spectral statistics of the BPS-projected operator display random-matrix behavior near the SYK (chaotic) limit and smoothly cross over to Poisson statistics near the integrable limit.
AI.conclusion: This provides a concrete example where chaos-integrability crossover can be diagnosed solely from BPS states, extending the framework of BPS chaos to detect dynamical transitions within protected subsectors.

title: Self-Consistent Parker Bound on Magnetic Monopoles
summary: Magnetic monopoles arise generically in unified theories and offer a natural explanation of charge quantization. Beyond collider searches and cosmic-ray experiments, their flux is constrained by Parker-type bounds requiring galactic magnetic fields to survive monopole energy extraction. We formulate a self-consistent Parker bound anchored in the lowest eigenmode of the galactic mean-field dynamo and convert the resulting limit to the present flux. Small-scale turbulent fields both seed this eigenmode and set the monopole velocity via stochastic acceleration before energy extraction from the coherent field. These unavoidable effects substantially modify the standard extended Parker bound at low and intermediate masses, yielding flux limits robust to primordial magnetic fields (PMFs); PMFs strong enough to alter them lie in regimes constrained by Ly$α$ data or testable by 21-cm and cosmological probes.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the Parker bound on magnetic monopole flux by incorporating the galactic mean-field dynamo's lowest eigenmode and the effects of small-scale turbulent fields on monopole acceleration, producing flux limits that are robust to primordial magnetic fields.
AI.motivation: To derive a self-consistent Parker bound on magnetic monopole flux that properly accounts for galactic dynamo physics and turbulent field effects, and to assess its robustness against primordial magnetic fields.
AI.method: The authors anchor the Parker bound to the lowest eigenmode of the galactic mean-field dynamo, model monopole velocity through stochastic acceleration from small-scale turbulent fields before energy extraction from the coherent field, and convert the resulting limit to present-day flux.
AI.result: The revised bound substantially modifies the standard extended Parker bound at low and intermediate masses. Primordial magnetic fields strong enough to alter the bound are already constrained by Lyα data or are testable with 21-cm and cosmological probes, making the new flux limits robust.
AI.conclusion: The self-consistent Parker bound provides more reliable monopole flux limits, and PMFs do not pose a significant threat to the bound's validity within observationally allowed regimes.

title: Wasserstein Space of Quantum Chaos
summary: We find that the effective dimension of the Wasserstein space of energy eigenstates decreases as a quantum system becomes more chaotic. To demonstrate this, we study a quantum coupled harmonic oscillator system using Husimi Q-representations, to which Sinkhorn-regularized optimal transport is applied to construct an embedding geometry via the Gram-spectrum method. We also demonstrate that exponential OTOC growth, referred to here as quantum scrambling even in the absence of chaos, induces a folding structure in the emergent Wasserstein space, which may underlie the chaotic reduction of the Wasserstein dimension. At the separatrix (the scrambling point) of the inverted harmonic oscillator, the Wasserstein distance correctly captures the Lyapunov exponent. Furthermore, we discover that a branching structure in the Wasserstein space signals quantum scar states within the chaotic sea of phase space. Our optimal transport approach thus provides a new diagnostic for quantum chaos, quantum scrambling, quantum scars, and quantum Lyapunov exponents. The observed chaotic dimensional reduction also supports the recent conjecture [arXiv:2604.17649] that the Wasserstein space serves as an emergent holographic space through the manifold hypothesis, since chaoticity is a characteristic signature of black holes in holography.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the effective dimension of the Wasserstein space of energy eigenstates decreases with increasing quantum chaos, using optimal transport on Husimi Q-representations of coupled harmonic oscillators. The approach captures Lyapunov exponents at the separatrix, reveals branching structures signaling quantum scars, and supports the conjecture that Wasserstein space is an emergent holographic space.
AI.motivation: To develop a new diagnostic for quantum chaos, scrambling, scars, and Lyapunov exponents using optimal transport geometry, and to test the conjecture that Wasserstein space serves as an emergent holographic space via the manifold hypothesis.
AI.method: Study quantum coupled harmonic oscillator system; use Husimi Q-representations; apply Sinkhorn-regularized optimal transport; construct embedding geometry via Gram-spectrum method.
AI.result: Effective dimension of Wasserstein space decreases as the system becomes more chaotic; exponential OTOC growth induces a folding structure in Wasserstein space; Wasserstein distance captures Lyapunov exponent at the separatrix; branching structure signals quantum scar states.
AI.conclusion: Optimal transport provides a new diagnostic for quantum chaos, scrambling, scars, and Lyapunov exponents. The observed chaotic dimensional reduction supports the conjecture that Wasserstein space is an emergent holographic space.

title: Exact Holographic Kinematics in AdS/CFT
summary: We propose that holography contains an exact kinematic sector distinct from holographic dynamics. The appropriate setting for this sector is a CFT on an open solid torus in the Weyl frame. The open solid torus introduces an intrinsic scale, and the Weyl frame makes this scale manifest as an extra bulk direction. The resulting bulk-boundary pairs are exact and finite: no cutoff, large-$N$ limit, strong-coupling assumption, or heavy-operator approximation is required. The AdS geometry appearing in this sector should be understood as a kinematic geometry; only in special CFTs and appropriate limits is it promoted to a dynamical semiclassical bulk. The standard boundary-anchored dictionary entries are recovered only as singular limits. As a striking demonstration, we show that Weyl-frame two-point functions provide a replica-free definition of entanglement entropy.

AI.tldr: Holography contains an exact kinematic sector where CFT on an open solid torus in the Weyl frame yields finite, exact bulk-boundary pairs without requiring cutoffs, large-N limits, strong coupling, or heavy-operator approximations. The AdS geometry here is kinematic, becoming dynamical only in special CFTs and limits. Standard dictionary entries emerge as singular limits, and Weyl-frame two-point functions offer a replica-free definition of entanglement entropy.
AI.motivation: To identify and formalize an exact kinematic sector within holography that is independent of standard approximations, and to demonstrate its utility in providing a replica-free definition of entanglement entropy.
AI.method: The paper places a CFT on an open solid torus in the Weyl frame, which introduces an intrinsic scale and manifests it as an extra bulk direction. This setup yields exact bulk-boundary correspondences without invoking typical holographic approximations.
AI.result: Bulk-boundary pairs are exact and finite without cutoffs or large-N/strong-coupling assumptions. AdS geometry in this sector is kinematic; standard holographic dictionary entries are recovered only as singular limits. Weyl-frame two-point functions define entanglement entropy without replica trick.
AI.conclusion: Holography has an exact kinematic sector, distinct from dynamics, where the AdS geometry is kinematic rather than dynamical. This framework provides a novel, replica-free definition of entanglement entropy and clarifies the conditions under which kinematic geometry becomes dynamical.

title: $B_c \to η_c$ form factors at large recoil: SCET analysis and a three-loop consistency check
summary: The double-logarithmic series of non-relativistic $B_c \to η_c$ form factors at large recoil is governed by a coupled set of integral equations, reflecting an intricate interplay between arbitrarily many soft-quark and soft-gluon exchanges. Whereas we previously derived these integral equations with diagrammatic resummation techniques, we analyze the form factors in the limit $m_b \gg m_c \gg Λ_{\rm QCD}$ with methods from Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) in this work. Although the resulting factorization theorem for the so-called soft-overlap contribution is known to be spoilt by endpoint divergences, it can still be used at the level of bare (regularized) quantities at any fixed order in perturbation theory. By calculating the required ingredients, we show that the SCET analysis confirms the predictions of the integral equations up to three-loop order. We also argue that the iterative structure and the intertwined soft-quark and soft-gluon effects can be derived from standard renormalization-group equations of the $B_c$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes, provided their inverse moments are regularized with an appropriate cutoff.

AI.tldr: This paper studies non-relativistic $B_c \to \eta_c$ form factors at large recoil using SCET, confirming earlier diagrammatic integral equation predictions up to three-loop order, and showing that the iterative soft-quark/gluon structure follows from renormalization-group equations of $B_c$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes with appropriately regularized inverse moments.
AI.motivation: To analyze the double-logarithmic series of non-relativistic $B_c \to \eta_c$ form factors at large recoil, where an intricate interplay between arbitrarily many soft-quark and soft-gluon exchanges occurs, using SCET methods to confirm and extend previous diagrammatic resummation results.
AI.method: Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET) factorization, bare (regularized) perturbation theory calculations, renormalization-group equations for $B_c$-meson light-cone distribution amplitudes with cutoff regularization of inverse moments.
AI.result: SCET analysis confirms the predictions of the previously derived integral equations up to three-loop order; the iterative structure and intertwined soft-quark/gluon effects can be derived from standard RG equations of $B_c$-meson LCDAs with appropriately regularized inverse moments.
AI.conclusion: Although the factorization theorem for the soft-overlap contribution is spoilt by endpoint divergences, it remains useful at the level of bare/regularized quantities at fixed order, and the SCET approach validates the integral equation framework to high perturbative order.

title: Matching $A$ with $F$ in long-range QFTs
summary: Unitarity is often a crucial ingredient in establishing theorems -- such as the $A$-theorem -- on the irreversibility of the renormalization group flow. The strongest thesis of this type of theorems would be that there exists a scalar function $A$ and a positive definite metric $G_{IJ}$ in the space of couplings such that the renormalization group flow satisfies a gradient equation, $\partial_I A= G_{IJ}β^J$, in which case $A$ is locally monotonic along the flow. In this paper we consider the long-range multiscalar $φ^4$ theory, which is a nonunitary model that is believed to be conformally invariant at fixed points, and show that its renormalization group flow satisfies the gradient structure up to the third loop order in the coupling. We also show that $A$ and $G_{IJ}$ can be matched to the leading nontrivial order with the sphere free-energy $\tilde{F}$ and Zamolodchikov's metric $C_{IJ}$ of the corresponding conformal theory concentrating on the examples of the long-range vector $O(N)$ and hypercubic $H_N$ models. Our results imply a perturbative proof of the $\tilde{F}$-theorem at the leading nontrivial order. We conclude the paper discussing briefly whether this result should hold to the next orders in perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the gradient structure of the renormalization group flow in long-range multiscalar φ⁴ theory, a nonunitary model, showing it satisfies a gradient equation up to third loop order, with A and metric G_{IJ} matching the sphere free-energy F̃ and Zamolodchikov's metric C_{IJ} in the O(N) and hypercubic H_N models, providing a perturbative proof of the F̃-theorem at leading order.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the renormalization group flow gradient structure (crucial for irreversibility theorems like the A-theorem) holds in nonunitary theories, specifically the long-range multiscalar φ⁴ model, which is conformally invariant at fixed points despite being nonunitary.
AI.method: Perturbative loop calculations up to third order in the coupling for the long-range multiscalar φ⁴ theory, matching the gradient function A and metric G_{IJ} to the sphere free-energy F̃ and Zamolodchikov's metric C_{IJ} in the O(N) and hypercubic H_N models.
AI.result: The RG flow satisfies the gradient structure up to third loop order in the coupling, and A and G_{IJ} match the leading nontrivial order of F̃ and C_{IJ} for the O(N) and H_N models, yielding a perturbative proof of the F̃-theorem at leading order.
AI.conclusion: The gradient structure holds perturbatively for this nonunitary model; the paper briefly discusses whether this result should extend to higher orders in perturbation theory.

title: Statistical sensitivity of neutrinoless double-beta decay exchange mechanism discrimination by tracking experiments
summary: Reconstruction of the individual energies and the opening angle between the electrons emitted in neutrinoless double-beta decay can probe the nature of the beyond-the-Standard-Model exchange mechanism that underlies the process. Although it is often stated that discrimination of the mechanism would require such measurements to be performed with high statistics, we show that this is not the case. If a single mechanism dominates the process, its discrimination at the 1$σ$ level is already achieved with just a few well-reconstructed events; only $\sim$10 such events are required to reach 3$σ$-level discovery sensitivity. In the presence of realistic reconstruction uncertainties, this requirement increases to $\sim$25 events, indicating that substantial discrimination power is retained as long as backgrounds remain small. We conclude that the pursuit of tracking detectors for exchange-mechanism discrimination remains valuable even for ``discovery-class'' experiments in which only a few signal counts are expected.

AI.tldr: Discrimination of the beyond-Standard-Model exchange mechanism in neutrinoless double-beta decay is possible with as few as ~10-25 well-reconstructed events, contrary to the common belief that high statistics are required.
AI.motivation: To challenge the prevailing assumption that discriminating the underlying exchange mechanism in neutrinoless double-beta decay requires high-statistics measurements, and to demonstrate that few well-reconstructed events suffice.
AI.method: Statistical analysis showing that with a single dominant mechanism, 1σ discrimination is achieved with just a few events, ~10 events for 3σ sensitivity, and ~25 events under realistic reconstruction uncertainties.
AI.result: Only ~10 well-reconstructed events are needed for 3σ-level discovery sensitivity; under realistic uncertainties this increases to ~25 events, provided backgrounds are small.
AI.conclusion: Tracking detectors for exchange-mechanism discrimination remain valuable even for discovery-class experiments with only a few expected signal events.

title: Causal UV completions of relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Relativistic hydrodynamics successfully provides an effective field theory description for the low energy regime of many out-of-equilibrium systems. On the other hand, in this paper we proof that any stand-alone hydrodynamic EFT is inherently acausal and therefore requires the addition of transient UV modes in order to restore causality. This is made possible by the exponential decay of dissipative hydrodynamics in a majority of the lightcone, allowing the possibility of a causal description that still reduces to the hydrodynamic one at late timescales. We then investigate the emergence and possible restrictions of the non-hydrodynamic modes in these causal UV completions.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that hydrodynamic effective field theories are inherently acausal and require transient UV modes to restore causality, enabled by the exponential decay of dissipative hydrodynamics within the lightcone.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the inherent acausality of stand-alone hydrodynamic EFTs and show that adding transient UV modes can restore causality while still reducing to hydrodynamics at late times.
AI.method: Mathematical proof of acausality in hydrodynamic EFTs, analysis of exponential decay properties within the lightcone, and investigation of non-hydrodynamic modes in causal UV completions.
AI.result: Stand-alone hydrodynamic EFTs are inherently acausal; causality can be restored by incorporating transient UV modes due to the exponential decay of dissipative hydrodynamics in most of the lightcone.
AI.conclusion: Causal UV completions of hydrodynamics are possible via non-hydrodynamic modes, which are explored for their emergence and restrictions.

title: Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-Handed Neutrino Loop
summary: We study cosmological collider (CC) signatures generated by right-handed neutrino loops in the setup of inflation combined with neutrino seesaw mechanism. We formulate the inflaton interaction with the right-handed neutrino through a unique dimension-5 operator respecting shift symmetry, which induces an effective chemical potential in the slow-roll background, leading to helicity-dependent right-handed-neutrino production and enhancing the CC signatures. The right-handed neutrino is described by two-component Weyl spinor with Majorana mass term. Using the Schwinger-Keldysh (SK) formalism, we derive a set of seed integrals for fermion propagators of the right-handed Majorana neutrino. With these we compute the factorized nonlocal contributions to the three-point inflaton correlator generated by the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop. We show that the chemical potential can substantially soften the heavy-mass Boltzmann suppression and amplify the oscillatory non-Gaussianity signatures associated with the dominant helicity mode. These provide a systematic framework for analyzing the fermion loop signatures in the cosmological collider physics and demonstrate that the heavy right-handed neutrinos associated with seesaw mechanism may leave observable imprints in the primordial non-Gaussianities.

AI.tldr: This paper studies cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops during inflation, using a dimension-5 inflaton-neutrino operator with shift symmetry, Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, and showing that an effective chemical potential enhances oscillatory non-Gaussianity by softening Boltzmann suppression, linking the seesaw mechanism to observable primordial non-Gaussianities.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether heavy right-handed neutrinos from the seesaw mechanism can produce observable cosmological collider signatures during inflation, potentially linking particle physics beyond the Standard Model with primordial non-Gaussianity observations.
AI.method: The authors formulate a dimension-5 inflaton-right-handed neutrino interaction respecting shift symmetry, treat the right-handed neutrino as a two-component Weyl Majorana fermion, and compute three-point inflaton correlators via the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, deriving seed integrals for fermion propagators and factorized nonlocal loop contributions.
AI.result: The chemical potential induced by the inflaton interaction enhances helicity-dependent right-handed neutrino production and substantially softens the heavy-mass Boltzmann suppression, amplifying oscillatory non-Gaussianity signatures from the dominant helicity mode.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a systematic approach to fermion loop CC signatures and demonstrates that heavy seesaw right-handed neutrinos can leave observable imprints in primordial non-Gaussianities.

title: Explicit Conditions for Diagnosing Tree-Level Unitarity
summary: We explicitly present all coupling conditions required for tree-level unitarity (tree unitarity) in theories with a finite number of massive and massless particles of spin up to 1. They allow us to diagnose tree unitarity of a system using only its particle content in the mass basis, without reconstructing the full Lagrangian. We show that all four-point amplitudes whose high-energy growth is canceled by tree unitarity conditions are on-shell constructible, thereby motivating the recursive construction of four-point amplitudes. By examining their high-energy growth, we derive tree unitarity conditions for four-point amplitudes. Imposing these conditions to simplify the Lagrangian structure, we use the Stückelberg formulation to derive the tree unitarity conditions arising from all higher-point amplitudes. We show that all tree unitarity conditions are fully captured up to five-point amplitudes, ensuring no necessity of examining higher-point ones. We apply our results to systematically examine tree unitarity conditions in the dark sector with a massive dark photon and dark matter particles of spin up to 1, and extract the essential features for mass generation in the massive dark photon case. In addition, we show that our results allow us to conclude that theories without scalars require an infinite tower of vectors and fermions for tree unitarity. Finally unitarity and related issues in the Higgs portal VDM are discussed in brief.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically derives tree-level unitarity conditions for theories with spin ≤ 1 particles, showing that all such conditions are captured by five-point amplitudes, and applies the results to dark sectors with massive dark photons and spin-1 dark matter.
AI.motivation: To provide a systematic framework for diagnosing tree unitarity in gauge theories using only particle content in the mass basis, without needing to reconstruct the full Lagrangian, and to understand unitarity constraints in dark sector models.
AI.method: The authors present explicit tree unitarity conditions for all four-point amplitudes, show four-point amplitudes are on-shell constructible under these conditions, use the Stückelberg formulation to derive higher-point conditions, and prove all conditions are captured up to five-point amplitudes.
AI.result: Tree unitarity conditions are fully captured up to five-point amplitudes; theories without scalars require infinite towers of vectors and fermions for unitarity; the framework is applied to dark photon and VDM models.
AI.conclusion: Tree unitarity in spin ≤ 1 theories can be diagnosed from particle content alone, with conditions saturated at five-point level, revealing essential constraints for mass generation in dark sectors and the necessity of scalars (or infinite towers) for unitary theories.

title: Sensitivity of the FCC-ee to axion-like particles at different center-of-mass energies
summary: The sensitivity of the proposed FCC-ee collider to axion-like particles (ALPs) is investigated at all planned center-of-mass energies, with focus on the case where the ALP couples primarily to electroweak gauge bosons at leading order. We study the associated production of the ALP with a photon, with the ALP decaying in turn to two photons, yielding a three-photon final state. The ALP coupling to the photon is evaluated for ALP masses of 5 to 320 GeV. In this effective model, the FCC-ee will be able to detect ALPs for couplings down to a few $10^{-6} \mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ ($10^{-5} \mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$) during the Z pole run (WW, ZH, and $t\bar{t}$ threshold runs). Additionally, this final state has the potential to probe the underlying electroweak structure of ALP couplings for ALP masses below the $Z$-boson mass.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the sensitivity of the proposed FCC-ee collider to axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple primarily to electroweak gauge bosons, focusing on a three-photon final state across all planned center-of-mass energies for ALP masses of 5-320 GeV.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the discovery potential of the FCC-ee collider for axion-like particles (ALPs) coupling to electroweak gauge bosons, particularly through the associated production with a photon and decay to two photons (three-photon final state).
AI.method: Study associated production of ALP with a photon, where ALP decays to two photons (three-photon final state); evaluate ALP-photon coupling for masses 5-320 GeV at all planned FCC-ee center-of-mass energies (Z pole, WW, ZH, and tt̄ threshold runs).
AI.result: FCC-ee can detect ALPs with couplings down to ~10⁻⁶ GeV⁻¹ at the Z pole run and ~10⁻⁵ GeV⁻¹ at WW, ZH, and tt̄ threshold runs.
AI.conclusion: The three-photon final state at FCC-ee provides strong sensitivity to ALPs, and can probe the electroweak structure of ALP couplings for masses below the Z-boson mass.

title: Gravitational Waves from Black Hole Reheating: The Scalar-Induced Component
summary: The reheating of the universe by the evaporation of light primordial black holes (PBHs) can leave a stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) background in the early Universe. In the monochromatic limit, their simultaneous evaporation produces an abrupt matter-to-radiation transition, triggering the so-called Poltergeist GW signal, usually predicted to be dominant and observable. We revisit this result by including the irreducible mass spread implied by gravitational collapse in General Relativity, whose infrared tail scales as $d f_{\rm PBH}/d\ln M_{\rm PBH}\propto M_{\rm PBH}^{3.78}$. We show that this minimal width smooths reheating enough to suppress the Poltergeist background by orders of magnitude, down to the level of the scalar-induced GW signal produced during a generic early matter era, such as one driven by the decay of a heavy relic. We provide a complete decomposition of the scalar-induced spectrum into eight production channels and find that none, except the one from PBH formation, reaches either the $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ bound or the projected sensitivity of future GW observatories. This reopens regions of ultra-light PBH parameter space previously thought to be excluded by these constraints.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds from primordial black hole evaporation, showing that including realistic mass spreads (with infrared tail scaling as M^3.78) suppresses the previously dominant Poltergeist signal by orders of magnitude. None of the scalar-induced GW channels reach observational bounds, reopening previously excluded ultra-light PBH parameter space.
AI.motivation: Previous work on PBH evaporation-induced GW backgrounds assumed monochromatic mass distributions, predicting a dominant, observable Poltergeist signal. This paper aims to test that result by incorporating the irreducible mass spread from gravitational collapse in General Relativity.
AI.method: The authors include the minimal mass spread from GR collapse (infrared tail d f_PBH/d ln M ∝ M^3.78) and perform a complete decomposition of the scalar-induced GW spectrum into eight production channels.
AI.result: The Poltergeist signal is suppressed by orders of magnitude due to the smoothed reheating transition. None of the eight scalar-induced channels (except PBH formation itself) reach ΔN_eff bounds or projected sensitivities of future GW observatories.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-light PBH parameter space previously thought excluded by GW constraints is reopened, as realistic mass spreads significantly weaken the predicted GW signals.
